model.title: Accelerating Access to Critical Therapies for ALS Reauthorization Act of 2026
model.meta: Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions Committee · Sen. Lisa Murkowski (R-AK)

summary.text: The bill would extend through fiscal year 2031 several federal programs that fund research into drugs and other therapies for amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS, also called Lou Gehrig's disease) and other neurodegenerative diseases. It would cover National Institutes of Health grants for studying experimental drugs for people who cannot otherwise join clinical trials, Food and Drug Administration grants for developing treatments, and a public-private partnership between the FDA and NIH to speed development and regulatory review of these treatments. The bill would also require NIH to review safety and effectiveness information when deciding whether to renew grants, require grantees to promptly report safety data from ongoing trials, and have NIH set the enrollment timeframe for those trials. Every five years, the FDA would have to publish a plan of actions to support safe, effective, and accessible experimental drugs for ALS and other rare neurodegenerative diseases, including a review of its past actions and recommendations for improvement. Finally, the Government Accountability Office and the Department of Health and Human Services would have to report on the impact of these grants.
